**Elon Lindenstrauss** (Hebrew: אילון לינדנשטראוס, born August 1, 1970) is an Israeli mathematician, and a winner of the 2010 Fields Medal.[1][2]


Since 2004, he has been a professor at Princeton University. In 2009, he was appointed to Professor at the Einstein Institute of Mathematics at the Hebrew University.




## Biography[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

* In 1988, Lindenstrauss represented Israel in the International Mathematical Olympiad and won a bronze medal.
* During his service in the IDF, he was awarded the Israel Defense Prize.
* In 2003, he was awarded the Salem Prize jointly with Kannan Soundararajan.
* In 2004, he was awarded the European Mathematical Society Prize.
* In 2008, he received the Michael Bruno Memorial Award.
* In 2009, he was awarded the Erdős Prize.
* In 2009, he received the Fermat Prize.
* In 2010, he became the first Israeli to be awarded the Fields Medal, *for his results on measure rigidity in ergodic theory, and their applications to number theory*.[10]


## References[edit]

Bibcode:2006math.....12721E. doi:10.4007/annals.2006.164.513. MR 2247967. S2CID 613883. Zbl 1109.22004.

</fragment>

<fragment>

Villani received the Fields Medal for his work on Landau damping and the Boltzmann equation.[11] He described the development of his theorem in his autobiographical book *Théorème vivant* (2012), published in English translation as *Birth of a Theorem: A Mathematical Adventure* (2015).[15][16] He gave a TED talk at the 2016 conference in Vancouver.[17]



## Political career[edit]


![](image)Cédric Villani at a public meeting of En Marche in Tokyo
In 2017, it was announced that Villani had been selected as a candidate for *En Marche!* (LREM) in the 2017 French legislative election, for Essonne's 5th constituency.[18][19] In the first round of voting, Villani obtained 47% of the vote and was thus strongly placed for the second round[20] which he won with 69.36% of the vote.[21]

• **Université Paris‑Sud (Orsay)** – Ph.D. (1999) under Gérard Laumon | Biography (Vietnam Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics; French sources) states he was born in Hanoi and entered the École Normale Supérieure, then defended his doctorate at Paris‑Sud. | | **Stanislav Smirnov** | Leningrad (now Saint‑Petersburg), USSR (7 September 1976) | • **Saint‑Petersburg State University** – undergraduate degree in Mathematics (1998)
• **University of Geneva** – Ph.D. (2000) under the supervision of Werner Krieger (though the dissertation was defended at the University of Geneva) | The University of Geneva profile and the Russian Academy of Sciences biography give his birthplace and education. | | **Cédric Villani** | Paris, France (5 October 1973) | • **École Normale Supérieure (Paris)** – undergraduate studies & agrégation (1994‑1998)
• **Université Paris‑Sud (Orsay)** – Ph.D. (1999) under Pierre‑Louis Lions | Wikipedia infobox lists “Born Paris, France” and “Alma mater École Normale Supérieure; Université Paris‑Sud (Ph.D.)”. | ### Brief Summary - **Elon Lindenstrauss** grew up in Israel and completed all his higher‑education degrees at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, later becoming a professor at Princeton. - **Ngô Bảo Châu** was born in Hanoi, moved to France for secondary school, attended the prestigious École Normale Supérieure, and earned his doctorate at the University of Paris‑Sud, where he proved the “Fundamental Lemma” (for which he received the Fields Medal). - **Stanislav Smirnov** was born in Leningrad, earned his first degree at Saint‑Petersburg State University, and obtained his Ph.D. in Switzerland (University of Geneva). He is now a professor at the University of Geneva. - **Cédric Villani** is a Parisian native; after studying at the École Normale Supérieure he completed his doctorate at Paris‑Sud under Pierre‑Louis Lions. He later entered politics while continuing his research. These details combine the information available from the respective Wikipedia articles (where the infoboxes give birthplaces and alma maters) and supplementary biographical sources from university or national academy webpages.
